description:
Location: crate-jmap-base-client/src/request.rs:174-192

  #[non_exhaustive]
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
  pub struct AccountInfo {
      /// Human-readable account name (e.g. the owner's email address).
      pub name: String,
      ...
  }

JMAP-sc1b.99 redacted Session's Debug impl to hide username and state, but explicitly deferred AccountInfo as a follow-up. The same PII concern applies: Session.accounts is HashMap<String, AccountInfo>, and Session's manual Debug impl surfaces the accounts map verbatim. Any {:?}-format of a Session walks into AccountInfo's derive(Debug) and prints AccountInfo.name, which the field's own doc-comment identifies as 'typically the owner's email address'.

This means the canary regression test added in .99 — which only verifies that the literal username field is redacted — does not catch the transitive leak through accounts. A future-proof tripwire test would put the canary email both in username AND in an AccountInfo.name value and assert it does not appear in {:?}.

Fix shape (mirror .99):
1. Drop Debug from AccountInfo derive.
2. Manual Debug impl that redacts 'name' to '[REDACTED]'.
3. Extend the .99 canary test (or add a new one) that puts the canary in both Session.username AND Session.accounts[key].name and asserts neither appears in the Debug output.

Why P3 not P2: same defense-in-depth class as .99. Transitive PII leak only fires when a caller Debug-prints a Session, which RFC 8620 doesn't recommend.
title: P3: AccountInfo derives Debug exposing 'name' (PII — typically owner's email)
